```{r}

k <- 5
n <- nrow(census.data)
folds <- sample(1:k, n, replace = TRUE)

linear_mse <- numeric(k)
glm_mse <- numeric(k)

for(i in 1:k) {
  test_index <- which(folds == i)
  train_data <- census.data[-test_index, ]
  test_data <- census.data[test_index, ]
  

  linear_prediction <- predict(linear_model, newdata = test_data)
  glm_prediction <- predict(glm_model, newdata = test_data)
  
  linear_mse[i] <- mean((test_data$House_value - linear_prediction)^2)
  glm_mse[i] <- mean((test_data$House_value - glm_prediction)^2)
}

mean(linear_mse)
mean(glm_mse)
```

```{r}
#polynomial
# Number of folds for cross-validation
cv_folds <- 5  # Set k = 5 for 5-fold cross-validation

# Function to perform cross-validation for polynomial regression (degree 1-5)
cv_polynomial <- function(data, y, folds = cv_folds) {
  mse_results <- numeric(5)  # Store MSE for polynomial degrees 1 to 5
  
  # Create a random split for cross-validation
  set.seed(123)  # For reproducibility
  n <- nrow(data)
  fold_indices <- sample(rep(1:folds, length.out = n))
  
  # Loop through polynomial degrees 1 to 5
  for (degree in 1:5) {
    fold_mse <- numeric(folds)  # Store MSE for each fold
    
    for (i in 1:folds) {
      # Split data into training and test sets
      test_indices <- which(fold_indices == i)
      train_indices <- setdiff(1:n, test_indices)
      
      train_data <- data[train_indices, ]
      test_data <- data[test_indices, ]
      train_y <- y[train_indices]
      test_y <- y[test_indices]
      
      # Create polynomial features for training and test data
      train_poly <- as.data.frame(lapply(train_data, function(x) poly(x, degree = degree, raw = TRUE)))
      test_poly <- as.data.frame(lapply(test_data, function(x) poly(x, degree = degree, raw = TRUE)))
      
      # Fit OLS model
      ols_model <- lm(train_y ~ ., data = train_poly)
      
      # Make predictions and calculate MSE for this fold
      predictions <- predict(ols_model, newdata = test_poly)
      fold_mse[i] <- mean((predictions - test_y)^2)
    }
    
    # Store the average MSE for the current degree
    mse_results[degree] <- mean(fold_mse)
  }
  
  return(mse_results)
}

# Apply cross-validation to find the best polynomial degree for your data
mse_results <- cv_polynomial(data = train_data[, c("Race", "Age", "Sex", "City", "Family_Size", "Total_family_income", 
                                                  "Years_in_the_United_States", "Usual_hours_worked_per_week", 
                                                  "Employment_status", "Total_household_income")], 
                             y = train_data$House_value, folds = cv_folds)

# Print the results and identify the best degree
print(mse_results)

# Best polynomial degree (with the lowest MSE)
best_degree <- which.min(mse_results)
cat("The best polynomial degree is:", best_degree)



```

```{r}
# Load necessary library
library(tree)

# Split the data into training and validation sets (50% split)
set.seed(123)  # Set a seed for reproducibility
train <- sample(1:nrow(census.data), nrow(census.data) / 2)
valid <- -train

# Fit the regression tree on the training set
tree_model <- tree(House_value ~ Race + Age + Sex + Family_Size + 
                   Total_family_income + Years_in_the_United_States + 
                   Usual_hours_worked_per_week + Employment_status + 
                   Total_household_income, data = census.data, subset = train)

# Cross-validation to determine the best tree size
cv_tree <- cv.tree(tree_model)

# Plot the cross-validation error to visualize which tree size is best
plot(cv_tree$size, cv_tree$dev, type = "b", xlab = "Tree Size", ylab = "Deviance")

# Get the best tree size from cross-validation (smallest deviance)
best_size <- cv_tree$size[which.min(cv_tree$dev)]
best_size

# Prune the tree based on the best tree size from cross-validation
prune_model <- prune.tree(tree_model, best = best_size)

# Make predictions using the pruned tree on the validation set
yhat <- predict(prune_model, newdata = census.data[valid, ])

# Compute Mean Squared Error (MSE) on the validation set
mse <- mean((yhat - census.data$House_value[valid])^2)

# Print the MSE for the pruned tree
cat("Test MSE for the pruned tree: ", mse, "\n")

# Plot the pruned tree
plot(prune_model)
text(prune_model)

```

```{r}
# Load necessary library
library(dplyr)

# Function to perform random train-test split and compute MSE for each cut
calculate_mse <- function(cuts, data) {
  # Create binned variables using cut
  data$Age_bin <- cut(data$Age, breaks = cuts, include.lowest = TRUE)
  data$Family_size_bin <- cut(data$Family_Size, breaks = cuts, include.lowest = TRUE)
  data$Total_family_income_bin <- cut(data$Total_family_income, breaks = cuts, include.lowest = TRUE)
  data$Years_in_the_United_States_bin <- cut(data$Years_in_the_United_States, breaks = cuts, include.lowest = TRUE)
  data$Usual_hours_worked_per_week_bin <- cut(data$Usual_hours_worked_per_week, breaks = cuts, include.lowest = TRUE)
  data$Total_household_income_bin <- cut(data$Total_household_income, breaks = cuts, include.lowest = TRUE)
  
  # Perform random train-test split (80% training, 20% testing)
  set.seed(123)  # For reproducibility
  train_index <- sample(1:nrow(data), size = 0.7 * nrow(data))  # 80% for training
  train_data <- data[train_index, ]
  test_data <- data[-train_index, ]
  
  # Fit the linear model
  model <- lm(House_value ~ Race + Sex + City + Employment_status + 
               Age_bin + Family_size_bin + Total_family_income_bin + 
               Years_in_the_United_States_bin + Usual_hours_worked_per_week_bin + 
               Total_household_income_bin, data = train_data)
  
  # Make predictions on the test set
  predictions <- predict(model, newdata = test_data)
  
  # Calculate MSE (Mean Squared Error)
  mse <- mean((predictions - test_data$House_value)^2)
  
  # Return the MSE
  return(mse)
}

# Test different numbers of cuts (bins)
cuts_range <- 2:10  # You can change the range as needed
mse_values <- sapply(cuts_range, function(cuts) calculate_mse(cuts, census.data))

# Output the MSE values for each number of cuts
mse_values
best_mse1 <- which.min(mse_values)
```
